stem: This dress is pretty, ____ it does not look good on me.
explain_zh: 前後語意相反（漂亮／不適合我），轉折連接詞要用 but。so 表結果、or 表選擇、if 表條件，語意都不合。記住：but 前後常是對比或出乎意料的結果。

stem: Getting up early on a cold morning is not easy, ____?
explain_zh: 動名詞片語（Getting up early...）當主詞時視為第三人稱單數 it。前句是 is not（be動詞否定），附加問句要用「be動詞肯定＋主詞」，故選 is it。

stem: Tonight I'll stay at the office until I ____ the work.
explain_zh: until 引導的時間副詞子句，要用現在式代替未來式，故選 finish。will finish 是常見錯誤，因為子句不能再用未來式。

stem: Charles ____ a day in the department store looking for a hat for his wife.
explain_zh: spend + 時間 + V-ing 表示「花時間做某事」，故選 spent。cost 的主詞通常是物品或費用而非人，saw、made 語意不合。

stem: Tom ____ ten pounds over the past two months. He looks much thinner now.
explain_zh: over the past two months 表示從過去持續到現在的一段時間，要用現在完成式 has lost。loses 是現在簡單式、will lose 是未來式，都與句意不符。

stem: I don't like any one of these three watches. Can you show me ____ one?
explain_zh: 三支錶都不喜歡，要求「再看一支其他的」，用 another one（不特定的另一個）。the others 需先有特定範圍、either 只能用在兩者之間，都不合適。

stem: The waiters are asked to be ____; they should always smile and remember to say "Welcome" and "Please."
explain_zh: 後文描述服務生要微笑、說歡迎光臨與請，這些都是有禮貌的表現，故選 polite。honest（誠實）、special、strong 都與服務態度無關。

stem: On Children's Day, Ms. Lee, a famous storybook writer, ____ to Molly's Bookstore to talk about her new book. My two little kids just can't wait to see her.
explain_zh: 後句 My two little kids just can't wait to see her 表示孩子們「迫不及待」，顯示作家來訪是尚未發生、令人期待的未來事件，故用 be going to 表示已排定的未來計畫 is going to come 最自然；came（已發生的過去式）、was coming、has come 皆與「尚未發生、令人期待」的語境不合。

tag_zh: 助動詞 do 代動詞
stem: No one thought James would appear at Katie's party. So when he ____, everyone was surprised and could not believe their eyes.
explain_zh: did 在此代替前面提到的 appear（出現），強調「他真的出現了」，故選 did。was、had 不能單獨代替 appear 這個動作動詞。

stem: B&J Café ____ known as the tallest building in town. However, O&G Restaurant became the tallest building in 2010.
explain_zh: 2010年被O&G超越之前，B&J「已經」是最高的建築，這個「更早的過去」要用過去完成式 had been。has been（現在完成式）和 is（現在式）都與後面「2010年被超越」的時序矛盾。

tag_zh: 關係子句省略關係代名詞
stem: Actor David Piper became tired of talking about the movie ____ after he was interviewed about it many times.
explain_zh: 完整關係子句應是 the movie that he is famous for，介系詞 for 的受詞關係代名詞 that 可以省略，故選 he is famous for。選項C的 that is famous for 缺主詞、不合文法。

NEWS HUNT   Kieran Hardy 11/07/2013
For years, we thought our Earth was the only blue dot up there.  Now another has been found.  Its name is HD189773b.  HD189773b is an exoplanet, a planet outside our Solar System, and is one of the nearest exoplanets to Earth.  Even so, ____.  Here's why: It is 63 light years away.  That means it is 370,440,000,000,000 miles from us.  Even if we fly at 3,500 miles an hour, it will take more than 12 million years to get there.
____: It is much bigger, it is made of gas and it is burning hot.  In heat as great as 1,000°C, life is not possible.  What is worse, it rains glass.  If 1,000°C does not kill you, glass rain will.
Even so, finding this blue giant ____.  It is the first time that we have been able to see the color of an exoplanet.  The color of a planet gives us ideas about what is happening on it.  While we have a long way to go before we find a new planet to live on, finding a blue dot is a good start.
stem: Even so, ____.  Here's why: It is 63 light years away.  That means it is 370,440,000,000,000 miles from us.
options: we cannot really call it a neighbor
we do not know anything about it yet
we might not be able to stay there for long
we are not sure how long it takes to get there
explain_zh: 後文說明距離遠到要飛1200萬年才能到達，因此稱不上是「鄰居」，故選 A。選項D與後文矛盾，因為文章已明確說出所需時間。

Lily: I like shopping and talking to people.  I think I can learn how to do business.  Maybe selling clothes is a good business for me.

I'll keep strong by playing my favorite sport, tennis, every day.  One day I'll join the national team and be another Lu Yen-Hsun.
stem: What question did the teacher most likely ask in class?
options: "What do you want to do in the future?"
"What's your plan for the coming vacation?"
"What do you like to talk about with your friends?"
"What's your favorite thing to do with your family?"
explain_zh: 四位學生都在描述未來想從事的職業或志向（做生意、寫程式、寫書、當選手），故老師的問題是關於未來規劃，選 A。

passage:
Here is the preface of Nick Foster's new book Married to Food.
My mother was lousy at cooking.  To her, cooking was more like an exciting experiment.  You put some of this and some of that in a pot, and you wait and see what will happen.  "No experiments, no experiences." is what she would say when her experiment did not turn out good, and I heard that a lot.
My father was a good cook, and he loved to cook, too.  He often said that he got my mother to marry him with a table of delicious food, not with a beautiful ring.  "A family needs only one good cook," he said.
Now I am a cook myself.  And I have my own restaurant.  I learned how to cook from my father, of course.  From him, I learned the art of cooking.  But I did learn one thing from my mother.  It's her famous saying: "No experiments, no experiences."
stem: What does it mean when someone is lousy at something?
options: They are not interested in it.
explain_zh: 後文說媽媽做菜像做實驗、常常「沒成功」，可知 lousy at 表「不擅長」，故選 B。與「有名」「感興趣」都無關。

Here are the rules for a game called "Trip to Dreamland."
1. Each player begins at START.
2. In each turn, first take one of the four cards (moon / snow / sun / drop) to decide how many spaces to move: moon for one space, snow for two spaces, sun for three spaces, and drop for four spaces.  Then follow the words next to the space you arrive at, if there is an instruction there.
3. The first one who gets to Dreamland wins the game.
Board path in order from START: START(0) -> Magic Fruit(1, move to Candy House) -> Dark Hill(2, go back to START) -> Candy House(3) -> Golden Bear(4, move to Light Church) -> Light Church(5) -> Lion King(6, move back 3 spaces) -> Gate Watchdog(7, stop and rest 2 turns) -> Dreamland(8, win).
stem: Below are the cards which four kids have taken since they began the game.  Who has won the game? (A) Anna: moon->sun->drop. (B) Kate: snow->sun->drop. (C) Billy: moon->snow->sun. (D) Ivan: snow->drop->moon.
explain_zh: 依序推算：Billy抽moon(1格)到Magic Fruit，被送到Candy House(第3格)；再抽snow(2格)到Light Church(第5格)；再抽sun(3格)恰好走到Dreamland(第8格)獲勝。其他三人推算後都停在Gate Watchdog或Candy House，未能抵達終點。

explain_zh: Lion King 上標示「Move back 3 spaces」，代表玩家一停在 Lion King 就會立刻被指示退回 3 格，不會停留在該格開始下一回合，故「永遠不可能從 Lion King 開始回合」為真，選 A；卡片只用來決定每回合走幾步，並未提到能決定誰先開始（B錯）；抽到 drop（4格）即可從 START 直接經 Golden Bear 被送到 Light Church，故第一回合就能到達 Light Church（C錯）；所有玩家都固定從 START 出發，卡片並不能決定起點（D錯）。

passage:
The idea may hit you once or twice a year.  You come home on a hot summer day, hoping to have a cool bath, and find out there is no water.  Then you see how important water is in your everyday life.  However, in many parts of the world, water is not just about one's everyday needs.
In countries like Tanzania, water is hard to get, and the job of collecting water falls on women's shoulders.  Girls are often kept home from school to collect water while their brothers stay at school studying.  Studies show Tanzanian girls who live 15 minutes from clean water spend 12% more time at school than those who live an hour away.  More time spent collecting water means less time for learning.  For these girls, "Knowledge is power" is not just words; it is a sad fact in real life.  With less time spent at school, their chances of getting well-paid jobs are small, and they often have no voice in important matters, like who to marry.  These girls are often married into poor families.  They have little money or knowledge to take care of their children, who often end up dying young.  For the baby girls who are lucky enough to live, their life may still center around "water," just like it did for their mothers.
stem: What does "The idea" mean in the reading?
options: Water is important in one's everyday life.
Water is not just about one's everyday needs.
It is nice to have a cool bath on a hot summer day.
We should not take a bath when there is little water.
explain_zh: 前段描述停水才驚覺水的重要，呼應 The idea＝水在生活中很重要，故選 A。C選項只是舉例情境，不是整句要表達的重點。

For these girls, "Knowledge is power" is not just words; it is a sad fact in real life.  With less time spent at school, their chances of getting well-paid jobs are small, and they often have no voice in important matters, like who to marry.  These girls are often married into poor families.  They have little money or knowledge to take care of their children, who often end up dying young.  For the baby girls who are lucky enough to live, their life may still center around "water," just like it did for their mothers.
stem: What can we know from the reading?
options: Children in poor countries die from drinking dirty water every day.
Girls who spend little time at school have a harder life when they grow up.
Girls in countries like Tanzania are often paid less for the same job than the boys are.
Children from poor families are often kept from school to take care of younger children.
explain_zh: 文中說少讀書會使女孩找不到好工作、無法自主決定婚姻，符合「少讀書的女孩長大後生活更辛苦」，故選 B。

(At Liz's birthday party)
Amber: Don't tell me you didn't go to Garden House.
Keith: Why would I go there?
Amber: For Liz's birthday cake!  I left you a voice message this morning!
Keith: But you said Matt would go to the bakery!  And why did you come here without me?  I was waiting outside your apartment for an hour!
Amber: No!  I said I'd have lunch with Matt, and we'd come straight here from the restaurant.  So I asked you to help get the cake after work.

Amber: My cellphone is dead!  I said in the message that you could call Matt's number if you wanted to find me.  Now please tell me you did bring the gift we got for Liz.
Keith: What gift?  I'm sure you didn't say anything about a gift in the message.
Amber: I told you that yesterday!
stem: What is Garden House?
explain_zh: 對話提到去 Garden House 是為了拿 Liz 的生日蛋糕（birthday cake），可知它是一間麵包店，故選 A。

passage:
Froggie was a frog who never remembered where he had been.  His biggest dream was to find the best pond to swim freely without worrying about water snakes.  One day, Froggie hopped to a kitchen and jumped into a pot full of hot water.  Froggie felt the burning heat and hurried out of the water as fast as his legs could carry him.  "I almost died there!" Froggie thought.
A few days later, Froggie went back to the same kitchen, totally forgetting he had been there.  He again hopped into the same pot.  This time, the water inside was cool.  He looked around and thought, "There's no water snake trying to eat me and I can have this place all to myself!"  At that moment, Froggie knew it was his dream pond.  What he didn't know was that the water was warming up over a low heat.
After thirty minutes of swimming, Froggie felt the water was warmer but he thought of this as a nice surprise.  "This sure is the best place for swimming.  I get to have a hot bath, too."  During his comfortable bath, the water kept getting warmer and warmer.  Froggie was so comfortable that he fell asleep.  And he never woke up.
stem: What lesson can we learn from Froggie's story?
options: Life is too short; one should live it to the fullest.
Those who use their time well will win in the end.
People are blind to problems that slowly get worse over time.
It is difficult to give up old habits, but easy to pick up new ones.
explain_zh: 水溫慢慢升高，青蛙卻渾然不覺、最後喪命，寓意是人常常忽略慢慢惡化的危機，故選 C。

passage:
These years churches are in a calamitous state.  To start with, the number of church-goers is dropping sharply (see Figure 1).  Many say they do not belong to any church, and those who do go less often than they used to.  Going to church appears less and less on people's to-do list.  Another worrying fact is that fewer and fewer young people go to church, which leads to an older church (see Figure 2).
And there is also the problem with money.  Keeping a church door open is not cheap.  Fewer people going to church means little money coming in.  This makes it harder to keep a church open.
When the time comes for a church to close, there is little to do but to sell it.  Churches that were lucky enough to find a buyer were put to other uses.  Some were changed into restaurants or school gyms, and some even became nightclubs, for example.  Churches that had little luck were knocked down in the end.
Just like a store that keeps losing business needs to think of ways to save itself, it is perhaps time for the church to try to win people's hearts back and play an important part in people's lives again.  This is not something that one can simply pray to get an answer to.
Figure 1 (percentage of church-goers by year): 1980:11%, 1985:10.2%, 1990:9.6%, 1995:8.5%, 2000:7.6%, 2005:6.8%, 2010:6%, 2015:5.2%, 2020:4.4%.
Figure 2 (average age of church-goers by year): 1980:37, 1985:39, 1990:40, 1995:41, 2000:43, 2005:47, 2010:51, 2015:54, 2020:56.
stem: What does it mean when someone is in a calamitous state?
options: They are looking for a second chance.
They lost interest in the outside world.
explain_zh: 後文列出信徒銳減、經費不足、教堂被拆等困境，calamitous state 指陷入嚴重困境，故選 A。
